fact.thing: share of stolen user assets Binance has replenished from its own funds
fact.claim: Binance says it has put back about 98% of the roughly $6.3 billion in user assets affected by the October 2026 hack, using its own money (its SAFU fund, part of its futures insurance fund, and its corporate treasury). That is not money taken back from the hackers. Binance is still buying the last 2%, which is less liquid tokens outside its top ten, and says users will not bear the loss. Withdrawals have been reopening in phases since November 1, one network and asset pair at a time, so check the withdrawal page or network status page for your coin.

sources.label: Binance Recovery Update #7 (2026-11-04)
sources.what: We have now replenished approximately 98% of the impacted amount, and we continue to buy the remaining token assets through market and OTC channels.

sources.label: Binance Recovery Update #7 (2026-11-04)
sources.what: Purchases for the remaining 2% are expected to be slower because these tokens are less liquid.

sources.label: Binance Recovery Update #6 (2026-11-03)
sources.what: Not all listed assets will become available at once. Like phase one, reopening will roll out progressively across the assets as security and readiness checks are completed. Deposit services remain open and are not affected.

sources.label: CNBC (secondary)
sources.what: Binance says it has restored backing for about 90% of the assets; that doesn't mean it has recovered 90% of the funds from the attacker.
